text:
nate: Heads-up — after the kernel-6.5 rollout in ap-east1 we've started seeing a cluster of hosts with GPU modules deferring probe and intermittent NCCL handshake timeouts. Provisioning backlog is spiking for P4/A100 capacity.

maria: Oof. Any early logs?

nate: Paste from one affected host: 
```
[  +0.123456] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel
[  +0.000123] nvidia: probe_defer or unresolved symbol: cgroup_attach_task_all?
[  +0.512345] nvidia: firmware: failed to load nvidia/xxx.ucode, -2
[  +1.234567] nvlink: link training failed, falling back
[  +2.345678] nvidia: NCCL handshake timeout between 10.0.0.23:22 and 10.0.0.45:22
[  +3.000000] oom-killer: invoked for process X (python)
```

aj: That probe_defer + unresolved symbol pattern smells like DKMS/kernel-headers mismatch on the DKMS build step — or a vmlinux symbol rename between 6.4 -> 6.5. We saw something similar when CUDA 11.8 landed with driver 525 on 6.5 in staging.

liz: Are these hosts running our standard image or a custom kube-provisioner flow? If it's the latter, initramfs updates might be missing and modprobe order could differ.

nate: Standard image (image-gpu-2025-03) but we did a mass kernel bump last night. DKMS logs in /var/lib/dkms show build failures on several hosts. Some hosts fell back to an older module but many ended up tainting the kernel and refusing the full driver.

sam: infra-bot just posted a deploy failure for the canary lab: "deploy/gpu-hosts: kernel-6.5 -> module build failed on 4/6 hosts" :warning:

infra-bot: CI: gpu-host-image-build #2245 failed: DKMS build step exited 2. See https://ci.internal/jobs/2245

maria: Impact: how much capacity is affected? Are A100 pools degraded or just P4s?

nate: Early numbers: ap-east1-a P4 pool ~18% hosts in probe_defer state, ap-east1-b A100 ~6% showing NCCL flakiness. Provisioning queue is up ~42 instances; autoscaler keeps retrying and hitting tainted hosts so effective available capacity is worse.

aj: Short-term mitigation options: 
- revert kernel rollout for ap-east1 to 6.4 image (rollback job queued)
- re-run DKMS builds manually on affected hosts after installing correct kernel-headers
- add a temporary routing policy to avoid scheduling to shaky hosts (pin stable nodes)
- fallback to driver 520 series if 525 is the culprit (need QA on perf)

liz: Revert has org-level impact but is safest. Rebuilding DKMS at scale is slow and risky; if headers mismatch across revisions we'll keep getting probe_defer.

maria: Cost/ops tradeoff — rollback costs time + transient risk to other services, but leaving capacity degraded pushes us to spin up extra on-demand capacity which will burn credits. Which is cheaper short term?

sam: Ops calc: spinning up on-demand P4s for the next 24h ~ $6k, rollback and re-validate across region ~ 4 engineers * 6h = 24 engineer-hours. Product impact if we keep degraded capacity is higher (queued jobs).

nate: Proposal: 1) Pause further kernel rollouts to other regions. 2) Kick rollback for ap-east1 canary and ap-east1-a pools only. 3) Mark affected nodes cordoned + add tainted node selector to avoid scheduling. 4) Parallel: create a DKMS repair job to attempt rebuild on nodes with matching headers (only where headers match). 5) Ops will spin up 6 temporary on-demand P4s to keep SLA while rollback verifies.

aj: I'll own the DKMS repair job (aj). Can someone file the rollback runbook?

liz: I'll open rollback runbook and start the rollback run. Oncall: please prepare a quickpost explaining expected window to CS.

maria: +1. Also add a TODO to increase canary size for kernel rollouts and add a post-deploy DKMS validation step.

sam: Noted — financial approval for on-demand burn granted for 24h.

nate: Thanks. I'll update the incident doc and schedule the rollback now. If you see hosts flapping, add logs to the incident thread. :thumbsup:

liz: rolling back ap-east1 canary now. ETA 45m.

aj: starting DKMS repair job on the list of nodes that have matching headers — I'll push status updates here.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-2043 "kernel-6.5 GPU probe_defer & NCCL timeouts — ap-east1" severity:high

maria: Great, keep the channel posted. If rollback looks clean, we need a follow-up runbook for kernel/header compatibility testing before any future mass rollouts.

nate: Agreed. Closing temporary triage — we'll continue updates in the incident thread.
